plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49]. The symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bidding strategy for n bidders with uniform values is to bid (n-1)/n times your value. With n=3, that's 2/3 of my value. My value is $22, so optimal bid ≈ $14.67. This balances winning probability against profit margin, maximizing expected long-run earnings.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $15, so I'll bid 15 × 2/3 = $10 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against competitors with lower values.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $10, so I should bid approximately 10*(2/3) = $6.7 to balance the probability of winning against overpaying, maximizing expected profit.
